posts.title: Oregon Ducks Up To No. 12 In CFP Rankings, Washington Cracks Poll At No. 24
posts.description: EAST LANSING, MICHIGAN - NOVEMBER 20: Dylan Raiola #8 of the Oregon Ducks celebrates his teammates second half touchdown run against the Michigan State Spartans at Spartan Stadium on November 20, 2026 in East Lansing, Michigan. (Photo by Gregory Shamus/Getty Images) Both the Ducks and Huskies are in the CFP Top-25 ahead of their rivalry clash Saturday in Eugene (4:30 p.m., NBC). Oregon moves up a spot to No. 12 after their blowout win at Michigan State while Washington checks in at No. 24 after their upset of Indiana. While the Ducks at-large odds increase slightly with the move, their best shot at the playoff remains via the automatic qualifier as Big Ten champion. Oregon is very likely to make the conference title game with a win Saturday over the Huskies. A loss all but eliminates Oregon from playoff contention. The Ducks are two-touchdown betting favorites over the Dawgs. November 2⃣4⃣ #CFP Top 25 https://t.co/Ax7mJPObI4 — CFP (@CFBPlayoff) November 25, 2026

posts.title: McLaughlin: Oregon Rolls And Gets Help From Washington
posts.description: EAST LANSING, MI - NOVEMBER 20: Dakorien Moore (1) of the Oregon Ducks reaches to make a one-handed 31-yard touchdown reception in the fourth quarter ahead of Charles Brantley (4) of the Michigan State Spartans during a college football game on November 20, 2026 at Spartan Stadium in East Lansing, Michigan. (Photo by Joe Robbins/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) By SPENCER McLAUGHLIN Contributor, 750 The Game.com Oregon never felt like they were going to lose to Michigan State. The Ducks walked away from East Lansing banged up on the field (Dierre Hill, Bear Alexander) but didn’t have to strain for their 45-7 win. That’s how it was supposed to play out. There honestly aren’t that many big picture takeaways from the way the Ducks performed on the field. Dylan Raiola wasn’t his best, but did more than enough to win the game for the Ducks–including another beautiful toss to Dakorien Moore for a 1-handed TD grab. posts.title: McLaughlin: Oregon Goes on Cruise Control vs Michigan
posts.description: EUGENE, OREGON - NOVEMBER 14: Quarterback Dylan Raiola #8 of the Oregon Ducks reacts after a touchdown during the first half of the game against the Michigan Wolverines at Autzen Stadium on November 14, 2026 in Eugene, Oregon. (Photo by Ali Gradischer/Getty Images) By SPENCER McLAUGHLIN Contributor, 750 The Game.com I wonder if the fine folks at ESPN College GameDay read my preview article last week, or if perhaps the comparison to Kyle Whittingham’s comments before Saturday’s game were plainly similar to those of Mike Gundy in 2025. Was Dan Lanning sending a message to the other sideline, the CFP Committee, or both when his team was trying to score with 2 minutes to play leading 28-7? My guess is more the latter, but we may never know for sure. Oregon took care of Michigan 31-7 on Saturday afternoon, in a game that was only that close because of self-inflicted mistakes by the Ducks.
